corpus.title: Order history with sorting and pagination
corpus.content:
Requirement: Order history with sorting and pagination

The buyer can open the order history page and see every past order in one table. Orders are listed newest first by default. The buyer can sort by order date, total price, and status. The table paginates ten orders per page. When an order ships, its status changes from processing to shipped and the updated status is visible on the order history page without a reload. The buyer can export the filtered table to CSV.

Acceptance criteria:
- Orders default to newest-first order date sort
- Sorting by total price is descending
- Pagination shows exactly ten orders per page
- Shipped status updates are visible on the order history page
- CSV export reflects the current filter and sort

Risk: high

corpus.title: Password reset flow
corpus.content:
Requirement: Password reset flow

A buyer who forgets their password can request a reset from the sign-in page. The request email contains a single-use link. The link expires after 30 minutes. Using the link signs the buyer out of any other sessions and forces a fresh sign-in.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reset link expires after 30 minutes
- A used link cannot be reused
- Other sessions are signed out after a reset

Risk: medium

corpus.title: Order history shows newest first and paginates
corpus.content:
Test case: Order history shows newest first and paginates
(type: functional, priority: high)

Preconditions:
- A signed-in buyer account with 25 seeded orders

Steps:
1. Open the order history page
2. Check the default sort order of the order table
3. Move to page two of the pagination control

Expected results:
- The newest order appears in the first row
- Page two shows orders 11 to 20

Requirement refs: REQ-001

corpus.title: Expired reset link is rejected
corpus.content:
Test case: Expired reset link is rejected
(type: negative, priority: high)

Steps:
1. Request a password reset
2. Open the reset link after it expires (30 minutes)

Expected results:
- The page shows an expired link message
- No password is changed

Requirement refs: REQ-002

corpus.title: API and business rules for demo-shop
corpus.content:
API and business rules for demo-shop

The REST API is mounted at /api/v1. Endpoints used by the UI:
- GET /api/v1/orders (params: sort, page, status)
- POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password
- POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password/confirm

Business rules:
- Discounts apply before tax; tax is computed on the discounted subtotal
- Refunds are accepted within 14 days of delivery
- Order totals are stored in cents, not dollars

Auth: Bearer tokens; reset links expire after 30 minutes.

corpus.title: Failure analysis: Exports the filtered table to CSV
corpus.content:
Failure analysis for e2e/order-history.spec.ts > Exports the filtered table to CSV

Category: product_defect
Root cause: the /api/v1/orders export handler ignores the page query param and streams all orders, so the export times out on the seeded 25-order dataset
Confidence: 0.9
Evidence:
- Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded
- Network: GET /api/v1/orders?export=csv took 31412ms
Suggested fix: paginate the export endpoint or stream it in chunks
